Covariate balance and overlap

Source: R/smdbal.R
smdbal.Rd

The standardised mean difference and variance ratio of each covariate between the treated and the controls, before and after weighting, with a verdict by a threshold; and the overlap of the propensity between the arms.

Usage

smdbal(x, d, w = NULL, ps = NULL, thr = 0.1)

Arguments

x

The covariates: a numeric matrix, a data frame or list of numeric columns, or one numeric vector, one row per unit.

d

The treatment: 0 or 1 (or FALSE or TRUE), two units in each arm at least.

w

NULL or weights from 0, one per unit (from cbatt(), say).

ps

NULL or the propensity of each unit, strictly between 0 and 1.

thr

The threshold of the verdict: one positive number.

Value

An object of class smdbal, a list: tab, one row per covariate (var, m1, m0, smd, vr, and with w also m1w, m0w, smdw, vrw); overlap, one row (min1, max1, min0, max0, out, wmax); bal; ovl; and thr.

Details

The standardised mean difference is (m1 - m0) / sqrt((s1^2 + s0^2) / 2) (Imbens and Rubin 2015): means weighted by w when given, the standard deviations always those of the unweighted arms, as 'cobalt' computes it by default, so that weighting moves only the numerator. The variance ratio is s1^2 / s0^2, weighted when w is given (with the unbiased correction for weights). bal is TRUE when every difference (weighted, with w) is below thr in absolute value; 0.1 is the usual rule.

Overlap (Cole and Hernan 2008): the propensity's range in each arm, the share of units outside the range both arms share (out), and the largest inverse probability weight (wmax); ovl is TRUE when no unit lies outside the common range. The propensity is the logistic regression of d on x unless ps gives it.

References

Imbens, G. W. and Rubin, D. B. (2015). Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences. Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/CBO9781139025751

Cole, S. R. and Hernan, M. A. (2008). Constructing inverse probability weights for marginal structural models. American Journal of Epidemiology, 168(6), 656-664. doi:10.1093/aje/kwn164

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- data.frame(age = rnorm(200, 40, 10), prior = rpois(200, 2))
d <- rbinom(200, 1, plogis((x$age - 40) / 10))
smdbal(x, d)
#> smdbal: balanced at 0.1: FALSE; overlap: FALSE
#>    var        m1        m0         smd        vr
#>    age 44.748673 36.687615  0.95167893 1.4812747
#>  prior  2.010989  2.119266 -0.07443683 0.7480863
#>        min1      max1       min0      max0  out     wmax
#>  0.07702527 0.9358613 0.04919905 0.7742637 0.09 12.98275
w <- cbatt(rnorm(200), d, x, est = "ebal", tgt = "att", reps = 0)$w
smdbal(x, d, w = w)$tab
#>     var        m1        m0         smd        vr       m1w       m0w
#> 1   age 44.748673 36.687615  0.95167893 1.4812747 44.748673 44.748673
#> 2 prior  2.010989  2.119266 -0.07443683 0.7480863  2.010989  2.010989
#>            smdw       vrw
#> 1 -8.388583e-16 1.9940894
#> 2 -3.052964e-16 0.6845163
